n: The Lord reigns, enthroned above the cherubim — the golden winged figures on the lid of the ark of the covenant. The proper response is trembling awe.

f.g: Cherubim (already plural in Hebrew): angelic guardians of God’s presence.

n: God is great in Zion, his chosen dwelling, and high above all peoples.
‘Terrible’ means awe-inspiring. The refrain ‘he is holy’ appears three times in this psalm (verses 3, 5, 9).
God is a mighty King who loves justice. He has established fairness and done what is right among Jacob’s descendants.
Worship at his ‘footstool’ — the ark of the covenant, or the temple, where God’s presence touches earth.

f.g: The ark or temple, pictured as the footrest of God’s heavenly throne.

n: Moses, Aaron, and Samuel are remembered as great intercessors who prayed for the people — and God answered.
God spoke to them from the pillar of cloud, and they kept his decrees.
God forgave his people yet still punished their wrongdoing. ‘Inventions’ means their evil deeds. Mercy and justice work together.
The final refrain calls for worship on God’s holy hill, Zion, ending on the theme of the whole psalm: the Lord our God is holy.
